html:
SMTO-FIL-0058 — SMTO can't remove a folder that still has files in it

GUID: 690fba4f-0aba-4734-9a69-702ac81b61b4
Slug: file-directory-not-empty
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: fil

What happened

  • SMTO was asked to remove a folder, but the folder still holds files or subfolders, or new ones appeared while SMTO was deleting. The folder itself was not removed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list everything inside the folder. You'll see which files are still there and whether you want to keep any of them.
  2. If you want the folder and everything in it removed, tell SMTO so clearly, for example "delete this folder and everything inside it". SMTO only removes a folder's contents when you ask, and checks every item first.
  3. If new files keep appearing in the folder, close the program that is adding them before trying again. Files that arrive during the removal leave the folder not empty.

What success looks like

  • The folder no longer appears when SMTO lists the folder that contained it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete files you haven't looked at just to empty the folder.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A directory removal failed with ENOTEMPTY (or Windows ERROR_DIR_NOT_EMPTY) because the directory still had entries, for example a non-recursive delete or entries created after the recursive preflight.

What this means

  • The OS returned ENOTEMPTY or Windows directory-not-empty status for an operation requiring an empty directory. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The OS returned ENOTEMPTY or Windows directory-not-empty status for an operation requiring an empty directory.

How to diagnose it

  • List current entries, including hidden ones, without assuming they are safe to delete.

How to fix it

  • List the directory's current contents and check changed_paths for entries already removed. Remove only authorized entries, or run a recursive delete (recursive=true, ideally after a dry_run) so a complete preflight covers every entry.
  • List the current directory contents. Remove only explicitly authorized entries or choose a supported recursive operation with a complete preflight.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended operation's emptiness requirement is met through explicitly authorized changes or a supported different operation.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass scope or ownership checks to force a larger operation through.
